If City is played first, playing a land on turn 2 sacrifices it, leaving only one land. The fetch land turn 1 into City turn 2 preserves City and maximizes mana. Playing Wooded Foothills or Bloodstained Mire turn 1 fetching a Mountain, then City of Traitors turn 2 gives RCC — enough for Engineer + Welder on turn 2.
annotations.actionTaken: Played City of Traitors as the turn 1 land drop.
annotations.betterLine: Play Bloodstained Mire or Wooded Foothills turn 1, fetch a Mountain, then play City of Traitors turn 2 for 3 mana (R + CC), enabling both Goblin Engineer and Goblin Welder on turn 2.

annotations.description: Soul-Guide Lantern's ETB trigger exiles a card from a graveyard. Gem25F Libby chose to exile Once Upon a Time (a spent instant with no further relevance) instead of Misty Rainforest. While neither card in the opponent's graveyard is immediately threatening, Misty Rainforest is a fetchland that could potentially be recurred (e.g., via Crucible of Worlds or Life from the Loam effects) and would provide actual mana fixing/thinning value if returned. Once Upon a Time is a cantrip that has already resolved and has essentially zero utility if somehow recurred. Exiling the fetchland denies more potential future value.

annotations.description: Cracking Bloodstained Mire here is suboptimal because it removes an artifact from the battlefield, reducing Goblin Welder's utility. Goblin Welder needs an artifact in play to swap with an artifact in the graveyard (like Urza's Saga or potentially Phyrexian Dragon Engine later). By sacrificing Bloodstained Mire, Libby loses the ability to sacrifice Soul-Guide Lantern to Goblin Welder to return an artifact from the graveyard. Additionally, the fetched Mountain is the second Mountain and doesn't enable anything new this turn since the existing Mountain is tapped. Keeping the Mire as a fetchland also provides flexibility to crack it at instant speed later or use it as Welder fodder. The Soul-Guide Lantern could have been activated instead to exile a card from Qwen3L's graveyard (Misty Rainforest) for minor value, or Libby could have simply cast Goblin Engineer or other spells first before deciding whether to fetch.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Bloodstained Mire to fetch a Mountain, sacrificing an artifact that could have been used with Goblin Welder.
annotations.betterLine: Keep Bloodstained Mire in play as a potential artifact for Goblin Welder to sacrifice. Instead, cast Goblin Engineer (using Mountain + Soul-Guide Lantern tap if needed) to search for Phyrexian Dragon Engine or another artifact, setting up Welder lines. Crack the Mire later only when the mana is actually needed.

More importantly, Raucous Theater enters tapped but provides surveil 1, which could put an artifact into the graveyard for Goblin Welder to swap with Soul-Guide Lantern or other artifacts. The Mountain is already tapped from the search, so entering tapped isn't a significant downside. Having access to black mana could also matter for future plays. However, since the player already has red mana and the immediate need is red, this is a relatively small optimization miss.

annotations.description: Casting Ignoble Hierarch during combat phase is suboptimal. The Hierarch should have been cast in the first main phase so that if Qwen3L ESPN wanted to attack with a creature (like activating Lair of the Hydra), the Hierarch's exalted trigger would be available. Additionally, casting creatures before combat rather than after is generally worse when you have combat tricks or want to hold up information, but here the Hierarch specifically has exalted which rewards being on the battlefield before combat. More importantly, casting Collector Ouphe would have been a much higher impact play - the opponent has Goblin Welder, Soul-Guide Lantern, and Lavaspur Boots, all artifacts with activated abilities that Ouphe shuts down. The Ouphe would neutralize a significant portion of the opponent's board.

annotations.description: Pithing Needle does not stop Collector Ouphe. Collector Ouphe has a static ability ('Activated abilities of artifacts can't be activated'), not an activated ability. Pithing Needle only prevents activated abilities of the named card from being activated. Naming Collector Ouphe with Pithing Needle accomplishes nothing — the Ouphe's static ability will continue to shut down all artifact activated abilities regardless. Meanwhile, the opponent has Wasteland (x2), Lair of the Hydra, and Verdant Catacombs with relevant activated abilities that Pithing Needle could actually name. More importantly, Grindstone is available as a search option and is the key combo piece (with Painter's Servant, presumably in the deck). Lotus Petal would provide immediate mana acceleration to help cast cards in hand like Goblin Engineer or Phyrexian Dragon Engine. Mishra's Research Desk could provide card advantage. Any of these would be more useful than a Pithing Needle naming a creature with only a static ability.

annotations.betterLine: Search for Lotus Petal to gain mana for casting Goblin Engineer (which can tutor Ensnaring Bridge from graveyard back to battlefield, or find other artifacts), or search for Grindstone as a combo piece. Pithing Needle naming Collector Ouphe is a complete whiff since the Ouphe's ability is static, not activated.

Making everything red doesn't help with any of these cards.

annotations.description: Painter's Servant is in the graveyard, not on the battlefield, so it doesn't make permanents any additional color. Casting Pyroblast targeting Collector Ouphe will do nothing because the Ouphe is green, not blue. The player incorrectly believes Painter's Servant is active and making things red/blue. This wastes a card for zero effect, and the Collector Ouphe continues to shut down the artifact plan.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Pyroblast (presumably targeting Collector Ouphe), believing Painter's Servant was on the battlefield making it a valid target
annotations.betterLine: Cast Phyrexian Dragon Engine as a 2/2 double striker that could potentially block or apply pressure, or activate Goblin Welder (though Collector Ouphe prevents artifact activated abilities). The correct plan would be to recognize Painter's Servant needs to be returned to the battlefield first before Pyroblast can work on non-blue permanents.

annotations.description: Pyroblast targeting Collector Ouphe will do nothing because Ouphe is green, not blue, and there's no Painter's Servant on the battlefield to change its color. This wastes a card for zero effect.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Pyroblast targeting Collector Ouphe (a non-blue permanent) before getting Painter's Servant into play.
annotations.betterLine: First activate Goblin Welder (a creature, unaffected by Collector Ouphe) to swap a dispensable artifact (like Pithing Needle) for Painter's Servant from the graveyard. With Painter's Servant in play choosing blue, Collector Ouphe becomes blue, and THEN Pyroblast would successfully destroy it.

annotations.description: At 2 HP with opponent at 14 HP, Libby declined to attack with any creatures despite having Phyrexian Dragon Engine (2/2 double strike = 4 damage unblocked), Painter's Servant (1/3), and Goblin Welder (1/1) against only one blocker (Collector Ouphe 2/2). Attacking with all three would force opponent to only block one, letting 4-5 damage through. Goblin Welder is currently useless as a combo piece due to Collector Ouphe shutting down artifact activated abilities.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to attack with any creatures
annotations.betterLine: Attack with all three creatures (or at minimum Phyrexian Dragon Engine and Painter's Servant) to deal 4-5 damage through the single blocker, pressuring the opponent's 14 life total while the combo is locked by Ouphe

annotations.description: At 2 life, tapped Ancient Tomb (dealing 2 damage, lethal) to cast Pyroblast targeting Collector Ouphe, which is green not blue. Without Painter's Servant on the battlefield, Pyroblast's 'destroy target permanent if it's blue' mode does nothing to a green creature. Even if they survived the life loss, the spell would accomplish nothing.
annotations.actionTaken: Tapped Ancient Tomb at 2 life to cast Pyroblast targeting the non-blue Collector Ouphe, killing themselves with Ancient Tomb's damage.
annotations.betterLine: If they wanted to cast Pyroblast, they should have exiled Simian Spirit Guide for {R} instead of tapping Ancient Tomb. More importantly, they needed to first cast Painter's Servant (choosing blue) to make Collector Ouphe blue before Pyroblast would work. Without Painter's Servant on the field, the correct play is likely to pass and try to survive behind Ensnaring Bridge.
